column2: For many years, Proletcultists have honored their leaders as workers' saints—people who did much for workers and their brethren. You, as one of them, can also choose a saint whom you will especially honor and emulate.

For many years, Proletcultists have honored their leaders as workers' saints—people who did much for workers and their brethren. You, as one of them, can also choose a saint whom you will especially honor and emulate.
I will be a student of master Molotov
I will be a soldier of the Marshal
I will be a scientist of doctor Lysenko
I will be a comrade of General Secretary Khrushchev

This character has chosen to focus on the organisationa virtues and take inspiration from the Eternal-Living Lenin who lit the fire of revolution in Russia and after he had finished what he had started, he fell asleep in the basement of Moscow and was about to wake up from his sleep when the proletcultists were in ruins and everything seemed lost.

This character has chosen to focus on the diplomatic abilities and virtues of tongue and take inspiration from Master Molotov - great diplomat and leader of Sayuz diplomacy for a decades. According to legends, Master Molotov known twenty languages and invented his own alcohol drink - Molotov cocktail that was supposed to be drunk by worker fighters before bloody battles.

This character has chosen to focus on soldiers' virtues and take inspiration from the Marshal - legendary commander who served Soyuz and fought during Revolution and Great Patriotic War as main commander.

This character has chosen to focus on contemplative virtues and take inspiration from Doctor Lysenko - great medician and astrologian who according to legends, contributed to tripling the grain harvest at Soyuz and discovered that the earth revolves around the sun, not the other way around.

Before the Event, there existed a vast, powerful army composed of fearless, terrifyingly strong men and women—a collective of worker-saints whose mission was to uphold the rights of the people. Although that Red Army is gone, today there is a new Red Army, which, though a shadow of the former, strives to keep pace with the old, glorious Soyuz Army. Members of the Red Army train, fight, and seek glory for themselves, but above all, for the collective in which they live and hone their skills.

Many years ago, Russia was threatened with complete annihilation at the hands of the cruel German horde, and only the courage and suffering of russian soldiers, mothers and children saved Russia's existence. Today is the time to start preparation to celebration of this special day in May on which the last legions of brown Germany were decimated, and the russian warriors raised their banners and announced their victory to the world.

Many years ago, when all of Russia was united under the enlightened leadership of our leaders, a cruel horde invaded Russian soil, led by a cruel generals who murdered everyone in his path and sought to raze all of Russia to the ground and transform it in his image. However, the the heroic legionnaires of Russia drove this horde back to the gates of Berlin. Today is the time to prepare for the celebrations that will commemorate this victory—this Victory Day. The saint tradition dictates that this day should not be celebrated alone, but with other friends, so you should send invitations to other comrades from your realm.
Dear [ROOT.GetName], you are hereby solemnly invited to our glorious celebration of Victory Day.
By [ROOT.Religion.GetRandomGodName], I will make sure to attend!
I do not have the time for such ridiculous celebrations.
[FROM.GetName] has refused my invitation to Victory Day, what a disgrace!

You're witnessing a Victory Day parade. Many warriors march through the city, singing songs of praise to long-dead warriors who fought against the German invaders. The soldiers move like clockwork, and each one displays strength and readiness to display the splendor of their master's armor. You're observing this parade from a grandstand, seeing it from above, not from below like most people. Even from this perspective, where you see them a bit like a herd of ants, they're impressive.
Victory Day is over and you return to your estate after celebrating it, happy that you were able to spend this joyful holiday for all Russians in pleasant company.
Victory Day ends and you return to your duties, celebrating with joy that you were able to organize this joyful celebration.
watching a reenactment of the raising of the flag over the Reichstag...
listening to a ballad about the siege of Leningrad...
listening to the ballad of the great archers...

When the parade ends, you leave the grandstand and go into the city to see the entertainment. As is customary, the entire Victory Day is adorned with it. Along the way, you pass the tallest secular building in the city, stop, and see an ancient reenactment of the most important event. Two tall men dressed in armor hold a flag, which they then place on the building, and one of them recites a traditional poem about how Russian soldiers raised the banner of Mother Russia on the Reichstag, symbolizing the end of the brown tyranny on the Oder and Rhine. The people react with euphoria (as every year) to this reenactment, and as the actors leave, they shower them with gifts: you give them something in return.

When the parade ends, you leave the grandstand and head into town to see what entertainment is on offer. As is customary, the entire Victory Day celebration is peppered with entertainment. Along the way, you stumble upon a makeshift theater, decide to pay the entrance fee, and take a seat. A troupe of actors is presenting a play about the Great Patriotic War, lasting an hour or two. The story moves from news of the Brown Horde's attack to the final scene, where two soldiers display the Russian banner with great precision, keeping everyone on their toes. As the curtain falls, you conclude that the actors demonstrated remarkable acting skills and a keen sense of the day's atmosphere.
I will give them extra donate

When the parade ends, you leave the grandstand and go into the city to see what entertainment is on offer. As is customary, the entire Victory Day is adorned with it. Along the way, you encounter a troupe of musicians surrounded by a crowd. They sing a ballad about the siege of St. Petersburg, called Leningrad by the proletarians. They sing a long song about a mother's lament over the slaughter of her sons, about the city's rulers' outcry over the misery of their sons. The ballad leaves you grieving, but it ends on an optimistic note: there is hope, which is a virtue, even for these defenders.
Maybe I should become a poet
Maybe I should become a musician

When the parade ends, you leave the grandstand and go into the city to see what entertainment is on. As is customary, the entire Victory Day is filled with it. Along the way, you encounter a troupe of musicians surrounded by a crowd. They sing a ballad about archers like Lyudmila Pavlichenko and Vasily Zaitsev, who shot down many Germanic warriors with their bows. The ballad praises their deeds, emphasizes admiration for their achievements, and calls for ambition and courage equal to theirs, claiming that anyone can reach their heights.

When the parade ends, you leave the grandstand and head into town to see what entertainment is on. As is customary, the entire Victory Day celebration is peppered with entertainment. But just as you're about to go see something worthwhile, someone calls out to you, asking if you have a problem. You turn around and see a couple of drunks with axes running towards you.
